v0.1.0November 1, 2026Documented prototype

A companion worth coming back to.

The first brief was a website game inspired by cozy virtual-pet experiences, with the café’s own cats at its heart.

THE FIRST SUNNY CORNER · OPEN FULL SCREENSHOT ↗

What we built

  • Pet, feed, play, and rest with three sample café cats.
  • Coins, food, medicine, wearable accessories, and two minigames: Purrfect pairs and Treat catcher.
  • Daily care goals, a digital café card, saved progress, and editable resident profiles.

The care loop

Needs fall over time, including while the player is away. Neglected cats become sick and need medicine, food, love, and rest before playtime returns. Coin games stay open during recovery so players can always earn medicine.

The next request

The interface worked, but the room needed depth, more direct interaction, and less space between controls.

The original 2D build was not committed before the 3D rewrite. Its screenshot and feature record are preserved here; we do not present a reconstructed build as an original source snapshot.

v0.2.0November 1, 2026Saved source

A room you can look around.

The room became the main experience. Smaller, translucent controls moved over a 3D space that guests could explore with a mouse or finger.

THE FIRST 3D ROOM · OPEN FULL SCREENSHOT ↗

What changed

  • An original 3D café with furniture, plants, a garden window, lighting, and shadows.
  • Drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, and keyboard controls with a reset-view button.
  • Stroking the cat replaced click-only petting, with a purring response and happiness gains.

A smaller interface

Care meters, daily goals, minigame shortcuts, and the companion dock became compact floating panels. A stroke that starts on the cat pets it; a drag that starts on the room moves the camera.

What we checked

Mouse hover strokes, touch-stroke handling, camera separation, cancelled gestures, second-touch handling, mobile layout, and the existing feeding and minigame flows.

View v0.2.0 source ↗

Original local source commit: 3bf556b7c04e. This was the first version saved in Git.

v0.3.0November 1, 2026Saved experiment

Finding the café’s voice.

The next pass added sound to everyday interactions. This was a useful experiment—and the feedback changed the direction of the following version.

THE SOUND EXPERIMENT · OPEN FULL SCREENSHOT ↗

What we tried

  • A higher-pitched synthesized purr.
  • Quiet UI clicks, feeding sounds, and a resting cue.
  • A generated café background with room noise and occasional cup clinks.

What the feedback told us

The purr sounded like buzzing, the feeding sound felt artificial, and the background read as white noise. The request was clear: use real cat recordings and café music, and remove the clinks.

What carried forward

A single mute control, safe sound startup, one purr voice instead of overlapping loops, and automatic audio pause when the browser tab is hidden.

View v0.3.0 source ↗

Original local source commit: 258fffc5b7d9. These experimental sounds belong to this historical version, not the current game.

v0.4.0November 1, 2026Saved gameplay build

Real sounds. A more natural companion.

We replaced the synthetic animal sounds with recordings, changed the background to relaxed café music, and gave the cat more natural details.

THE MORE NATURAL COMPANION · OPEN FULL SCREENSHOT ↗

What changed

  • Real recorded purring and feeding replace the synthesized animal effects.
  • Kevin MacLeod’s relaxed Bossa Antigua replaces the white-noise background. No added cup clinks.
  • A smaller adult-cat model with fur texture, glossy irises, fine whiskers, slimmer forelegs, and more natural proportions.

Making it feel calmer

The music plays quietly and dips while cat sounds play. Playback uses short, gently faded excerpts, with source credits available inside the game. The room controls, minigames, care economy, and saved progress stay in place.

What we verified

Recorded MP3 assets and playback, excerpt loading, mute safety, background-tab pause, coats and accessories, and mouse/touch petting. The browser loaded the music and cat recordings without playback errors.

View v0.4.0 source ↗

Original local source commit: b28a64e182a4. Recording and music licenses travel with the source in dist/audio/credits.json.

v0.5.0November 2, 2026Current build

Meet Little Beans Cat Cafe.

The prototype gets its café identity and 17 residents from the supplied Little Beans poster. The home expands around the player, with clear controls floating over it.

LITTLE BEANS COMES HOME · OPEN FULL SCREENSHOT ↗

What changed

  • The supplied logo and Little Beans Cat Cafe name appear in navigation and on the room’s wall.
  • All 17 named cats have reference-photo portraits and individual care progress.
  • The floor and room surfaces extend around the camera. The floating-platform border and blank outer space are gone.
  • Clearer panels reveal the room underneath. Petting uses a hand cursor.

Interpreting the references

Seated 3D models now have a continuous torso, finer face proportions, physical guard hairs, detailed irises, and coat variations based on the photos. The small poster supports approximate markings, not faithful hyperrealistic reconstruction. Higher-resolution multi-angle references and custom 3D work are still needed for that level of likeness.

Progress carries forward

The three placeholder cats’ care progress moves to the closest matching residents: Mochi to Zeus, Olive to Ralph, and Luna to Star. Coins, inventory, accessories, daily goals, and café-card progress are retained. New residents start with healthy care values.

View v0.5.0 source ↗
STILL A PROTOTYPE, WITH ROOM TO GROW

The next little chapter.

Improve each resident’s 3D likeness with detailed reference photography. Connect bookings and staff-verified visits. Carry progress between devices. The current café card is a digital prototype, not a verified in-person loyalty program.
